thread:
maya-support: Hey team, we just got a high-priority ticket from a customer (acct: acme-ux) — their embeddings requests are showing huge tail latency and some vectors landed in the EU region even though they set region=us-west-2 in the SDK. They're seeing timeouts in their downstream vector DB (timeout at 5s).

alex-cs: Thanks for flagging — customer says it started around 08:05 UTC and correlates with a big batch job they ran. Request IDs: r-8f3a2c9e and r-8f3a2d00. They included a curl they used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' \
  -H 'X-Region: us-west-2' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-huge-1536","input":["a","b","c"]}'
```

maya-support: We reproduced quickly — some requests routed to eu-west-1 which caused ~600ms extra cold-starts and others stayed in us-west-2. Also saw a couple of `dimension mismatch` logs when the client expected 1024 dims but the model returned 1536 for a fallback variant.

cheng-platform: Hmm. Did the SDK set `region` or `X-Region`? We respect `X-Region` header but the routing layer can spill to another region if local capacity exhausted. Need logs for the routing decision: request_id r-8f3a2c9e.

routing-bot: Routing log for r-8f3a2c9e: selected_region=eu-west-1 reason=capacity_spillover capacity_score_local=0.23 capacity_score_remote=0.78 model_variant=embed-huge-1536 fallback_variant=embed-large-1024

eva-sre: Copying the routing log fragment I see `fallback_variant=embed-large-1024` — that explains the dimension mismatch. When the runtime falls back to a 1024-dim model but the client expects 1536 the vector DB ingestion step fails. We should avoid silent fallback for embeddings; that should return 4xx or explicit `fallback_applied` header.

maya-support: Customer reports their ingestion pipeline failed with error: `invalid_vector_size: expected 1536 got 1024` — so some requests did silently switch models. They'd like a reproducible test to show how/when the spillover happens.

cheng-platform: Repro steps for infra team:
1) Use the customer's API key (or a synthetic key mapped to their account) and send a sustained stream of embeddings requests to us-west-2 (concurrency ~120, qps ~200) with `model=embed-huge-1536`.
2) Monitor routing decisions in the control plane logs (`/var/log/routing/*.log`) and watch for `capacity_spillover` within time window.
3) Check `autoscaler` metrics for us-west-2 zone: `gpu_pool_utilization`, `queue_length`, and `cold_start_rate`.

Example load command: 
```
hey -n 10000 -c 200 --header "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \
  --header "X-Region: us-west-2" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
```

ops-bot: Alert created: #INC-2026 embedding routing spike — linked to thread 1925001111. Notifying eng-sre and eng-platform.

eva-sre: I ran a quick check of the autoscaler logs around 08:04-08:12 UTC; looks like a spike in new connections triggered scale-up but there was a ~45s window where we had insufficient warmed workers and the router started sending traffic to eu-west-1 to keep latency SLOs. Cold-start penalty ~550-700ms.

cheng-platform: That aligns. Two issues: 1) silent model fallback causes dimension mismatch and downstream failures; 2) region spillover without a visible flag makes debugging hard for customers. Proposals: add `X-Fallback-Applied: true` header when fallback occurs, and introduce an opt-in strict-mode `X-Strict-Region: true` which will return 429/5xx instead of routing if local capacity is unavailable.

maya-support: Customer approves strict-mode for them — they prefer errors over silent rewrites. Can we set it as an account-level switch while we fix autoscale?

cheng-platform: Yes, we can toggle `strict_region` on the customer record; that bypasses automatic spillover for their key. I'm assigning to @cheng-platform to flip and monitor.

alex-cs: Also the customer wants logs showing when cold-starts happened. Can we provide a short timeline and per-request routing headers?

routing-bot: Sample headers returned to client for r-8f3a2c9e: 
```
X-Routed-Region: eu-west-1
X-Fallback-Variant: embed-large-1024
X-Cold-Start: true
X-Routing-Reason: capacity_spillover
```

maya-support: Perfect. I'll send these headers and the repro steps. Also include recommended mitigations for them: reduce concurrency bursts, enable local batching (we saw their client sent many parallel single-item calls rather than batching 16 per request), and pin `X-Strict-Region` while we stabilize.

cheng-platform: For infra tasks:
- eva-sre to investigate why warm pool size didn't cover the burst — check warm_pool_target and scale_cooldown settings for us-west-2.
- cheng-platform to add header flags and account-level strict toggle.
- eng-runtime to reject silent embedding fallbacks (should return 409 incompatible-model or a clear `fallback_applied` status).

eva-sre: On it. I see warm_pool_target was lowered in last week's tweak to reduce costs; that change made us more vulnerable to short spikes. Rolling back warm_pool_target to previous value should reduce cold-start incidence, but we need to watch cost impact. I'll open a PR and mark for emergency roll.

maya-support: ETA to share workaround with customer?

cheng-platform: I can flip `strict_region` for acme-ux within 10 minutes and add `X-Fallback-Applied` to the router responses in staging now; production deploy for header will take ~2 hours after review.

alex-cs: Customer wants a writeup for SOC/compliance showing region assurance. Please include: timeline, exact routed-region headers, and the permanent fix plan (autoscaler warm pool rollback + strict-mode option + non-silent fallback).

maya-support: I'll draft the customer note once cheng confirms the toggle.

ops-bot: Deploy started: platform/region-routing-headers (PR #4082) — staging build 2026-03-15T09:02:00Z.

eva-sre: Rolling back the warm_pool_target change now (PR #4079). Deploying to us-west-2 as emergency: expected impact <5m, warm pool should increase from 6->12 nodes.

cheng-platform: Flip done for acme-ux: `strict_region=true` on their API key. Please verify with them that they now get 429 instead of cross-region routing during a controlled replay.

maya-support: Customer confirmed after test they now receive `429 RegionCapacityExceeded` and no requests routed to EU. They ran their ingestion and proceeded more slowly. They accepted the mitigation for now.

alex-cs: Closing loop items:
- [x] Toggle strict_region for acme-ux (cheng-platform)
- [x] Provide routing headers and request timeline (maya-support)
- [ ] Permanent fix: non-silent fallback + header in prod (cheng-platform / eng-runtime) — in progress
- [ ] Warm pool rollback monitoring (eva-sre) — in progress

maya-support: Thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread open for postmortem notes and cost impact details. :pray:

cheng-platform: I'll follow up with a small postmortem and signal the need for a safer warm_pool change process (include canary metrics for cold-start rate).

ops-bot: Alert resolved: #INC-2026 — status: mitigated (strict-region enabled)

maya-support: Marking last_message_ts here.
